title: Quick technical gut-check — Ashwin Kapoor (candidate)
text:
Quick, messy brain dump after pairing + system-design loop with candidate Ashwin Kapoor (applied to Runtime SDE). Not polished — personal impressions, numbers for quick compare, and suggested follow-ups.

Interview context:
- Date: 2025-11-03 (pairing + whiteboard + short coding exercise).
- Interviewers: Samir Patel (owner/author), Leah Morgan (observing), Diego Ramos (follow-up).
- Candidate background (from resume + convo): 5 years infra + ML infra at VoltAI, led an inference infra team for CPU/GPU autoscaler; prior role included hooking a custom KV cache into a transformer-serving pipeline. Familiar with CUDA basics, Rust for tooling, and some JAX/Flax exposure.

High-level impression (TL;DR):
- Strong infra instincts; thinks in operational failure modes and tradeoffs.
- Moderate to strong systems-design skills for inference (caching, routing, autoscaling).
- Coding: solid but not flashy — wrote clear code, some micro-optimizations missing.
- Not deep on low-level attention kernel math or quantization tricks (would need upskill for kernel-level perf wins).

What we covered / questions asked:
1) Prefix/KV cache design for multi-tenant hosts: asked for data structures, eviction, mem usage accounting, and hot-key handling. Candidate sketched a shard-per-model cache, LRU-ish with frequency counters, async eviction to avoid tail latency — good practical answers.
2) Serving path: described request flow (ingest -> routing -> model shard -> KV lookup -> batched forward). Could explain backpressure and how to drop requests during overload.
3) Latency SLO edge cases: asked to handle long sequence lengths and cold cache penalty; suggested fallback to smaller model variant + partial responses. Nice pragmatic thinking.
4) Coding exercise: implement simplified rolling window aggregator (30m). Candidate wrote readable code, missed an edge case (integer overflow for counters over long time windows) — fixed with small hint.
5) Kernel/quantization deep-dive: when I probed for quantization-aware attention packing, answer was surface-level (has used 8-bit quant libs, but not built kernels).

Behavioral / ownership / collaboration notes:
- Communicates clearly; good at surfacing unknowns ('I haven't implemented that kernel but this is how I'd approach').
- Mentions leading small cross-functional launches (infra + product), comfortable doing on-call and postmortems.
- Asks good clarifying questions during prompts, pragmatic about deadlines.

Rubric (1-5; 5 highest):
- System design (inference/runtime): 4
- Production judgment (SLOs/on-call/alerts): 4
- Coding (correctness + clarity): 3
- Low-level performance (kernels/quantization): 2
- Mentorship/communication: 4
- Overall fit for Senior Runtime SDE: 3.5 (leaning towards hire for Mid+/Senior with growth plan)

Major strengths:
- Practical infra-first mental model; prioritizes requests by business-level SLOs and cost tradeoffs.
- Comfortable with multi-tenant constraints and isolation; proposed sensible routing fallback policies.
- Good communicator and likely to partner well with SRE and infra teams.

Concerns / gaps:
- Not currently a kernel-level optimization expert; may take time to land 20-40% token-cost/latency wins from low-level work.
- Limited exposure to advanced quantization pipelines and custom CUDA kernels.
- Coding exercise showed small gaps in edge-case thinking under time pressure — likely fine with a short pairing ramp.

Red flags: none acute. No behavioral miscues. Technical gaps are addressable depending on role level expected.

Suggested hiring outcome / next steps:
- Recommend: Proceed to take-home or focused pairing on performance path (2-hour exercise): implement a small in-memory KV cache (sharded) with eviction and a simple bench harness to show tail-latency under hot-key scenario. Goal: observe candidate's ability to think about concurrency and memory accounting.
- Alternative: move to final on-site with emphasis on kernel/quantization pairing if role requires immediate kernel work.
- If we hire, plan: place on infra/product-impact projects (routing & caching) with a 3-month kernel mentorship plan (pair them with an applied-ml/runtime engineer for quant/kernels).

Concrete follow-ups (my todo):
- Draft pairing exercise prompt (due 2025-11-08). Leah to review.
- If candidate agrees to take-home, schedule within 7 days.
- Save candidate's GitHub (linked above) and check for prior small PRs that touch CUDA/numba.
- Post summary to Slack channel #hiring-runtime with rubric + recommendation.

Small notes for interview packet / hiring committee:
- Candidate scores well on prod judgement and infra primitives. Would be a good addition if we value shipping reliable inference quickly.
- If comp/level aligns with our Senior expectations (kernel autonomy), we should either raise the bar in follow-up or consider as Senior+ but with kernel ramp plan.

Random micro-observations (brain dump):
- Candidate repeatedly used 'async drains' for eviction to avoid head-of-line blocking — liked that framing.
- Suggested per-tenant soft quotas rather than strict hard limits; good for PLG customers to avoid noisy neighbors but requires clear billing signals.
- Mentions previous work improving median latency via batching strategy changes (shard-by-model + micro-batching) — ask for metrics in follow-up.

Decision snapshot: Hold for targeted take-home focusing on concurrency & memory accounting. If take-home passes, recommend hire at Senior (level depends on comp discussion).

End of note.
